name: Ember Summit
geological_features: A single mega-volcano dominating one hemisphere
Concentric lava terraces descending from the summit
Ash deserts on the opposite hemisphere
specific_features: Energy readings from within the mega-volcano that pulse in regular intervals
description: Ember Summit is dominated by a single volcanic structure of almost incomprehensible scale. The mega-volcano rises forty kilometers above the surrounding terrain, its summit perpetually wreathed in fire and toxic fumes. Concentric terraces of cooled lava descend its flanks like the steps of a titan's amphitheater, each one hundreds of meters tall.

From the ash deserts of the far hemisphere, the mega-volcano is visible as a dark mass on the horizon, its summit glow painting the clouds in shades of amber and crimson. The air tastes of metal and sulfur even at the greatest distance from the peak. Earthquakes are constant, their rhythms tied to the volcano's deep internal cycles.

Microbial life clings to existence in the cooler ash deserts, but the volcano's increasing activity is shrinking their habitat with each eruption cycle. More puzzling are the energy readings from deep within the mega-volcano, which pulse at regular intervals suggesting a source that is not purely geological. Multiple theories have been proposed, none satisfactorily.

Ember Summit's exotic matter signatures, emanating from the volcano's core, have made it a priority target for deep-survey missions. The challenge of reaching the source through kilometers of active volcanic material remains unsolved. Some researchers believe the regular energy pulses indicate an artificial source buried within the mountain, possibly predating the volcano itself.
